title: Blocked Pawn Positions
description: Learn how to handle blocked pawn structures: passed pawns, blockading pieces, and the critical role of king activity in locked positions.

sections.title: The Blocked Pawn Chain
sections.content: When pawn chains lock the position, the game often becomes a struggle for king activity. The side with the more active king can create threats on the weak side of the chain. The general rule: attack on the side where your pawns are blocked.

positions.commentary: A blocked pawn chain. White's e5 pawn is blocked by black's e6 pawn. In such positions, the king should march to the opposite wing to create a passed pawn or exploit weaknesses.
hints: The king should go to the opposite wing from the block
Look for pawn breaks or weaknesses on the flanks

sections.title: The Blockading Piece
sections.content: A blockading piece (usually a knight or bishop) sits in front of a passed pawn, preventing its advance. The blockader is a double-edged sword: it stops the pawn but can become a target. To break the blockade, use your king to attack the blockading piece.

positions.commentary: White knight blocks the black e-pawn. This is a classic blockade. The knight is well-placed, but the black king should try to attack it. If the knight is forced away, the pawn advances.
hints: The blockading knight controls d3, f3, c5, f5, d7, f7, c3, f3
Bring your king to attack the blockader

sections.title: Zugzwang in Blocked Positions
sections.content: In blocked positions, the side to move often faces zugzwang — any move worsens their position. This is especially common in king and pawn endings where the defending king must maintain a precise square. Force the opponent to move first to win.

positions.commentary: White to move. This is a zugzwang position. If white moves the king, black gets the opposition. The key is to maintain the opposition and force black to yield.
hints: Maintain the opposition — keep your king opposite the black king
Zugzwang means the opponent must move first, worsening their position

exercises.title: Opposition in Blocked Position
exercises.description: White to play. Use the opposition to force black's king away and create a passed pawn.
hints: Take the opposition — move your king to face the black king
The goal is to force black's king to move away

exercises.title: Attack the Blockader
exercises.description: Black to play. The white knight blocks your e-pawn. Can you attack it with your king?
hints: Move your king toward the blockading knight
If the knight is forced away, the pawn advances
